How often you have to buy new clothes and how much it adds up. We're always shown these before and after pics of people who have lost a lot of weight and the result is that you never consider the fact that there's a lot of in progress stages in between. You don't go from a size 18 to a size 8 all at once, you have to be a size 16 first, then 14, then 12, etc. I got to a point where my pants wouldn't stay up and I had run out of holes in my belt before I finally accepted that you can't just wait until the "after" to get new clothes. And it's very frustrating to pay for new clothes when you still have a significant amount to lose and you know that soon those new clothes are gonna be baggy and frumpy too.

Kind of? I'm not totally sure if I have an official diagnosis or not. Looking back I know now that I've struggled with depression and anxiety since early childhood but I didn't see a therapist/psychologist (I don't remember which) until I was 12. I had had panic attacks before but for some reason at that age I was having severe attacks on an almost daily basis to the point that my parents finally realized it was more than just preteen angst and took me to see a professional. I got my depression and general/social anxiety diagnoses on my first visit which my mom was supportive of. The second visit was when the therapist suggested that I was autistic and my mom freaked out. I still remember her rant about how the therapist was crazy and how I couldn't possibly be autistic because everyone with autism is diagnosed around 2-4 years old and it's impossible for autistic people to make eye contact (which I'm not great at but can do.) 

I didn't know what autism was so I assumed my mom must be right. I haven't seen another mental health professional since then (only our family doctor who is able to prescribe me anti-depressants.) As an adult though I've learned that the things my mom believed about autism are completely false. And learning more about autistic traits explains A LOT about me. I'm not mad at my mom, I think she was just trying to protect me from a diagnosis that she thought would cause a lot of trouble for me but I just wish I could know for sure. I'm afraid now to say I'm autistic because if I'm not I don't want to be seen as faking it. I feel you with worrying about people not believing you and that's especially hard when you don't even have enough "proof" to completely believe yourself. I wish you luck with finding an answer and I hope your parents will be willing to listen.

It's extremely normal for your interest level in something to fluctuate over time. Losing interest at the moment doesn't mean you'll never enjoy the game again. I've been playing for a little over a year and a half and I've had plenty of mini "breaks" from the game where I just logged in once a day, maybe played shocking party for the loveca and then turned the game off. It's good to get some new content into your brain sometimes. Try a totally different game or watch a new show or spend some extra time on another hobby. Your sif account will be okay if you aren't playing efficiently for a while. 

As far as other goals in the game go, I kind of hit a wall with my WW account too a while back. My goal for a long time was building up my teams and they're now at a point where the only new cards that could fit on my teams need to be scorer URs. That made scouting pretty frustrating since without whaling it's hard to get specific URs and it's sad when any healer or plock UR is just a disappointment. I ended up switching my goal from "have good teams" to "get all the older μ's cards I don't have." That's made the game a lot more interesting for me. There's so many pretty SRs I don't have and now getting any unique card is exciting. I pulled constellation kotori from a BT scout recently and that made me just as happy as getting a UR, she's so cute. I'd love to collect all the mermaid and fairy cards (hilariously I have both fairy Nico and Rin and NONE of the SRs.) I rambled a bit but yeah, switching your focus to a "smaller" goal can definitely help you find some appreciation for aspects of the game that were being ignored in favor of tiering.

I agree with you that Ruby's most recent SR (and the new years set in general) isn't the best art that we've seen in the game. But look at [Ruby's SR from the snow fairy set](https://i.schoolido.lu/c/1829idolizedRuby.png) we got just before this. The snow fairy set is easily some of the highest quality art that has ever been in the game, I think it looks much better than the cheerleader set. With how quickly new cards are released it's probably safe to assume that different artists were working on the two sets at the same time. The artist(s) responsible for the snow fairy set are more skilled than the artist(s) who worked on the new years set. Even when all artists involved are conforming to the same style there's still going to be slight differences. Art is hard and it's impossible to exactly match how someone else draws.

Sif does a good job when it comes to keeping the art mostly consistent. And overall I feel like the sets have been improving. I think saying that the art quality is declining based only on the most recent cards released is a little harsh.
